claims.text: Aid can finance essential services when local public resources are limited, supply technical knowledge and provide relief after a shock. A grant avoids repayment, but donor conditions or poorly chosen projects can reduce local control or usefulness. Foreign investment can provide equipment, jobs, training and market connections. Profits may leave the economy, local suppliers may be bypassed, and weak safeguards can leave pollution or poor work conditions. Loans can spread payment for useful capacity over time but commit later resources to debt service. Judge feasibility, local influence, maintained benefits and opportunity cost for each arrangement; a larger inflow is not proof of greater welfare.
